title: Decimal Fractions: Place Value, Comparing, Rounding and Converting
seo_title: Grade 6 Decimal Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, order and compare decimal fractions to at least 2 decimal places; round off decimal fractions to at least 1 decimal place; recognise the place value of digits in decimal fractions to at least 2 decimal places; recognise and use equivalent forms of common fractions and decimal fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 decimal fractions worksheets: place value, comparing and ordering, rounding off and changing fractions to decimals. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths after the decimal comma.
key_sub: Line up the commas, then compare from the left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • After the decimal comma come tenths, hundredths and thousandths: 3,457.
  • 0,5 = 510, 0,05 = 5100, 0,005 = 51000.
  • To compare, line up the decimal commas and compare from the left. 0,6 > 0,48.
  • To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit.

Examples

Example

Order 0,6; 0,48; 0,605

0,600; 0,480; 0,605

Answer: 0,48; 0,6; 0,605

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Longer is bigger0,48 < 0,6.
Wrong place0,3 is 3 tenths.
The wrong digitLook one place to the right.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about decimal fractions?
faq.a: Recognise, order and compare decimal fractions to at least 2 decimal places, round off decimal fractions to at least 1 decimal place, and recognise the place value of digits in decimal fractions.

faq.q: Why does South Africa use a decimal comma?
faq.a: It is the South African standard: 2,5 means two and a half.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in this number?
items.e: The 3 is the 1st digit after the point, in the tenths place. Its value is 3 tenths = 3 × 110 = 0,3.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in this number?
items.e: The 4 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 4 hundredths = 4 × 1100 = 0,04.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in this number?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so its value is 7 × 10 = 70.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in this number?
items.e: The 8 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths = 8 × 1100 = 0,08.

items.q: In 5,55, how does the 5 in the tenths place compare to the 5 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The tenths 5 is 0,5 and the hundredths 5 is 0,05. 0,5 = 10 × 0,05, so it is worth 10 times as much. One place to the left is always 10 times as much.

items.q: In 3,333, how does the 3 in the thousandths place compare to the 3 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The thousandths 3 is 0,003 and the hundredths 3 is 0,03. 0,003 is 0,03 ÷ 10, so it is worth 110 as much. One place to the right is always 110 as much.

items.q: What is 10 times as much as 0,03?
items.e: 10 times as much moves each digit 1 place to the left: 3 hundredths become 3 tenths, 0,3. Writing a 0 at the end (0,030) does not change the value.

items.q: What is 110 of 0,4?
items.e: 110 of a number moves each digit 1 place to the right: 4 tenths become 4 hundredths, 0,04. (4 is 10 times as much, and 0,40 is the same as 0,4.)

items.q: 0,6 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: 10 times what is 0,6? One place to the right of tenths is hundredths: 0,06. Check: 10 × 0,06 = 0,6.

items.q: How many hundredths are in 0,3?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths. 0,3 = 0,30.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4,307?
items.e: The red 7 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 7 thousandths = 0,007. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 6,054?
items.e: The red 5 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 5 hundredths = 0,05.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 13,582?
items.e: The red 5 is the first digit after the decimal point, in the tenths place. Its value is 5 tenths = 0,5.

items.q: In 9,473, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: After the decimal point the places are tenths (4), hundredths (7) and thousandths (3). So the hundredths digit is 7.

items.q: In 21,509, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: After the decimal point: tenths 5, hundredths 0, thousandths 9. The thousandths digit is 9.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0,7?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 0,7 = 0,70 = 0,700. 0,07 and 0,007 have the 7 in a different place.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0,4?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 4 tenths = 400 thousandths. 0,4 = 0,400.

items.q: Write 0,045 as a fraction.
items.e: 0,045 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 45 thousandths = 451 000. 45100 would be 0,45.

items.q: In 3,33, the 3 in the tenths place is worth how many times the 3 in the hundredths place?
items.e: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 0,3 = 10 × 0,03. So the answer is 10.

items.q: What number is 0,1 less than 8,04?
items.e: Take away 1 tenth. 8,04 has 0 tenths, so regroup 1 one as 10 tenths: 8,04 − 0,1 = 7,94. 8,03 takes away 1 hundredth.

items.q: Compare 0,45 and 0,5.
items.e: 0,5 = 0,50. Compare the tenths: 4 tenths < 5 tenths. So 0,45 < 0,5. More digits does not mean a greater number.

items.q: Compare 0,6 and 0,58.
items.e: 0,6 = 0,60. Compare the tenths: 6 > 5. So 0,6 > 0,58.

items.q: Compare 3,08 and 3,080.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 3,08 = 3,080, so 3,08 = 3,080.

items.q: Compare 0,007 and 0,07.
items.e: 0,07 = 0,070. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 7. So 0,007 < 0,07. 7 thousandths is less than 7 hundredths.

items.q: Compare 0,99 and 1,01.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 0 < 1. So 0,99 < 1,01. Any number less than 1 is less than any number greater than 1.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,600; 0,590; 0,599; 0,065. Compare the tenths first: only 0,6 has 6 tenths. So 0,6 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,304; 0,340; 0,400; 0,430. The least is 0,304, even though it has the most digits.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0,3 to 0,4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth (0,01). Count 7 spaces on from 0,30: 0,37.

items.q: Compare 0,125 and 0,13.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0,125 and 0,130. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 2 < 3. So 0,125 < 0,13. Do not compare 125 with 13.

items.q: Compare 4,216 and 4,21.
items.e: 4,21 = 4,210. Ones, tenths and hundredths are the same. Compare the thousandths: 6 > 0. So 4,216 > 4,21.

items.q: Compare 0,5 and 0,45.
items.e: 0,5 = 0,50. Compare the tenths: 5 tenths > 4 tenths. So 0,5 > 0,45. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

items.q: Compare 0,38 and 0,4.
items.e: 0,4 = 0,40. Compare the tenths: 3 < 4. So 0,38 < 0,4.

items.q: Compare 2,07 and 2,070.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 2,07 = 2,070, so 2,07 = 2,070.

items.q: Compare 0,009 and 0,09.
items.e: 0,09 = 0,090. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 9. So 0,009 < 0,09. 9 thousandths is less than 9 hundredths.

items.q: Compare 0,98 and 1,02.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 0 < 1. So 0,98 < 1,02. Any number less than 1 is smaller than any number greater than 1.

items.q: Compare 0,405 and 0,45.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0,405 and 0,450. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 5. So 0,405 < 0,45.

items.q: Compare 3,125 and 3,12.
items.e: 3,12 = 3,120. Ones, tenths and hundredths are the same. Compare the thousandths: 5 > 0. So 3,125 > 3,12.

items.q: Compare 1,9 and 1,899.
items.e: 1,9 = 1,900. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 9 > 8. So 1,9 > 1,899.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,205; 0,250; 0,300; 0,520. The smallest is 0,205, even though it has the most digits.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0,5; 0,45; 0,405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,500; 0,450; 0,405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0,405; 0,45; 0,5.

items.q: Round 3,46 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 3,46 is between 3,4 and 3,5. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 3,5.

items.q: Round 7,38 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 7,38 is between 7 and 8. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 3. 3 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 7.

items.q: Round 2,735 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 2,735 is between 2,73 and 2,74. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 2,74.

items.q: Round 0,65 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 0,65 is between 0,6 and 0,7. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 0,7.

items.q: Round 4,96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 4,96 is between 4,9 and 5,0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 4,9 + 0,1 = 5,0. Answer: 5,0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: Round 3,995 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 3,995 is between 3,99 and 4,00. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. The hundredths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 3,99 + 0,01 = 4,00. Answer: 4,00. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the hundredth.

items.q: Round 6,849 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 6,849 is between 6,8 and 6,9. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 6,8. Do not round in steps (6,849 → 6,85 → 6,9). Look only at the hundredths digit.

items.q: Round 0,462 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 0,462 is between 0,46 and 0,47. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 2. 2 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 0,46.

items.q: Round 12,508 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 12,508 is between 12 and 13. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 5. 5 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 13.

items.q: Round 9,96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 9,96 is between 9,9 and 10,0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 9,9 + 0,1 = 10,0. Answer: 10,0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: Round 0,073 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 0,073 is between 0,0 and 0,1. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 0,1.

items.q: A swimmer's time was 14,387 seconds. What is the time rounded to the nearest hundredth of a second?
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 14,387 is between 14,38 and 14,39. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 14,39.

items.q: Musa's pencil is 17,65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimetre?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17,65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: A puppy weighs 4,548 kg. What is its weight rounded to the nearest tenth of a kilogram?
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 4,548 is between 4,5 and 4,6. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 4,5. Do not round in steps (4,548 → 4,55 → 4,6).

items.q: A runner finished a race in 58,249 seconds. What is the time to the nearest tenth of a second?
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 58,249 is between 58,2 and 58,3. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 58,2. Do not round in steps (58,249 → 58,25 → 58,3).

items.q: A scale shows 6,482 kg. A label rounds it to 6,5 kg. To which place was it rounded?
items.e: 6,5 has one digit after the point, so it is rounded to the nearest tenth: 6,482 is between 6,4 and 6,5, and the hundredths digit is 8, so it rounds up to 6,5. To the nearest hundredth it would be 6,48, and to the nearest whole number 6.

items.q: Bongani's pencil is 17,65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimetre?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17,65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: Zinhle's pencil is 17,65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimetre?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17,65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: Elna's pencil is 17,65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimetre?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17,65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: Zanele's pencil is 17,65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimetre?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17,65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: Write 0,3 as a fraction.
items.e: 0,3 has one decimal place, so the 3 is in the tenths place: 3 tenths = 310.

items.q: Write 0,71 as a fraction.
items.e: 0,71 has two decimal places, so it is hundredths: 71 hundredths = 71100. 7110 would be 7,1.

items.q: Write 0,09 as a fraction.
items.e: Two decimal places means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0, so 0,09 = 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Write 29100 as a decimal.
items.e: 29 hundredths: the last digit goes in the second place after the point. 29100 = 0,29.

items.q: Write 0,045 as a fraction.
items.e: 0,045 has three decimal places, so it is thousandths: 45 thousandths = 451 000. 45100 would be 0,45.

items.q: Write 0,007 as a fraction.
items.e: 0,007 has three decimal places, so the 7 is in the thousandths place: 71 000. 7100 would be 0,07.

items.q: Write 2,3 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 2 wholes, then 0,3 = 3 tenths. So 2,3 = 2 310. 2 3100 would be 2,03.

items.q: Write 3 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 3 wholes and 7 tenths. Tenths are the first place after the point: 3,7.

items.q: Write 2,09 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 2 wholes, then 0,09 = 9 hundredths. So 2,09 = 2 9100. 2 910 would be 2,9.

items.q: Write 5 6100 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 wholes and 6 hundredths. The 6 must be in the second place, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 5,06.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4,073?
items.e: The red 7 is in the hundredths column, the second place after the decimal point. Its value is 7 hundredths = 0,07.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2,508?
items.e: The red 8 is in the thousandths column, the third place after the decimal point. Its value is 8 thousandths = 0,008. Thousandths are the third place, not the second.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 13,264?
items.e: The red 2 is in the tenths column, the first place after the decimal point. Its value is 2 tenths = 0,2.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 0,719?
items.e: The red 9 is in the thousandths column, the third place after the decimal point. Its value is 9 thousandths = 0,009. Thousandths are the third place, not the second.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 3,456?
items.e: In 3,456 the 6 is in the thousandths place (3rd after the decimal point). So its value is 6 thousandths = 0,006.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in 5,638?
items.e: In 5,638 the 3 is in the hundredths place (2nd after the decimal point). So its value is 3 hundredths = 0,03.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 9,104?
items.e: In 9,104 the 4 is in the thousandths place (3rd after the decimal point). So its value is 4 thousandths = 0,004.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 12,875?
items.e: In 12,875 the 8 is in the tenths place (1st after the decimal point). So its value is 8 tenths = 0,8.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0,239?
items.e: 0,239 has three decimal places, so the last digit is in the thousandths place: 239 thousandths = 2391 000.
The 5 is in the hundredths place, so it is worth 5 hundredths = 0,05. Check: 6 + 0,2 + 0,05 + 0,004 = 6,254.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0,3 to 0,4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. Count 8 spaces on from 0,30: 0,38.

items.q: Which point shows 2,07?
items.e: Each space is 0,1. 2,07 is less than 2,1, so it sits before the first tick: point A. Point C is 2,7.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 2,1 to 2,2 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. Count 4 spaces on from 2,10: 2,14.

items.q: How much is each space on this number line worth?
items.e: 0,7 − 0,6 = 0,1. Split 0,1 into 10 equal spaces: each space is 0,01 (1 hundredth).

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are only 5 spaces from 0 to 1, so each space is 0,2 (1 ÷ 5). The dot is 3 spaces along: 0,2; 0,4, 0,6. 0,3 counts the spaces as tenths.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: From 1 to 1,1 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. 9 spaces on from 1,00 is 1,09. 1,9 would be much further along, near 2.

items.q: Which point shows 0,35?
items.e: Each space is 0,01. 0,35 = 0,30 + 5 hundredths, so it is 5 spaces along: point C. Point A is 0,305, halfway between 0,30 and 0,31.

items.q: What number is halfway between 0,3 and 0,4?
items.e: 0,3 = 0,30 and 0,4 = 0,40. Halfway between 30 and 40 hundredths is 35 hundredths: 0,35.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are 4 spaces from 1 to 2, so each space is 0,25 (a quarter). The dot is 3 spaces along: 1,25; 1,5, 1,75.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: There are 5 spaces from 0,4 to 0,5, so each space is 0,1 ÷ 5 = 0,02. The dot is 2 spaces along: 0,42, 0,44. 0,42 counts each space as 0,01.

items.q: Pieter ran 3 710 km. Write this distance as a decimal.
items.e: 3 whole kilometres and 7 tenths: 3,7 km. 3,07 would be 3 and 7 hundredths.

items.q: Thandi’s water bottle holds 0,75 ℓ. Write this as a fraction of a litre.
items.e: 0,75 has two decimal places, so it is hundredths: 0,75 ℓ = 75100 ℓ.

items.q: The school rain gauge showed 15,4 mm on Monday, 9,8 mm on Tuesday, 15,2 mm on Wednesday and 4,6 mm on Thursday. Which day had the most rain?
items.e: Compare the whole numbers first: 15 > 9 > 4. Then 15,4 > 15,2 (4 tenths > 2 tenths). So Monday had the most rain.

items.q: At the athletics day, the long jump results are: Kabelo 3,05 m, Ethan 3,5 m, Sibusiso 3,15 m and Dumisani 3,4 m. Who jumped the furthest?
items.e: Write them with 2 places: 3,05; 3,50; 3,15; 3,40. The greatest is 3,50 m, so Ethan jumped furthest.

items.q: Palesa is 1,4 m tall. Her brother is 1,39 m tall. Who is taller?
items.e: 1,4 = 1,40. Compare the tenths: 4 > 3. So 1,40 m > 1,39 m and Palesa is taller.

items.q: Chloe swam 50 m in 40,5 seconds. Ayanda swam 50 m in 40,50 seconds. Who was faster?
items.e: 40,5 = 40,50, because a 0 at the end does not change the value. So they tied.

items.q: Tebogo swam 50 m freestyle in 41,27 seconds. What is the value of the digit 7?
items.e: 41,27: the 7 is the second digit after the point, so it is 7 hundredths of a second (0,07 s).

items.q: Lwazi cuts four pieces of ribbon: 1,5 m, 1,455 m, 1,05 m and 1,505 m. Which piece is the longest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 1,500; 1,455; 1,050; 1,505. The greatest is 1,505 m, 5 thousandths longer than 1,5 m.

items.q: Mum buys 0,375 kg of cheese, 0,4 kg of ham, 0,35 kg of salami and 0,25 kg of olives. Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,375; 0,400; 0,350; 0,250. The greatest is 0,400 kg: the ham.

items.q: A builder has two boards. One is 1,205 m long and the other is 1,25 m long. Which board is longer?
items.e: 1,25 = 1,250. Compare the hundredths: 5 > 0. So 1,250 > 1,205 and the 1,25 m board is longer.
